map-lxxii-192.summary: Louis XII has ordered Bourbon into Burgundy with lances and Landsknechte; news of a rout has overturned a plan; the king is angry at people who yielded to the English; the English king has shipped his baggage and his army is embarking, part of it at Calais; the king says he is secure and will fight if the Swiss move; the prelates leave for Rome after All Saints.
map-lxxii-192.en:
The holes are those of the Italian reading: [...] an unread word, [?word] a word proposed for signs that do not spell it, [15], [?26], [?47] numbers with no value. Words in which the Italian brackets a single letter or a second key value ([B]orgogna, [bene]) are translated without the mark; they are holes in the count all the same.

In a postscript to my last, of the 20th, I told Your Lordships that the Most Christian King, in assigning the garrisons, had ordered Monsieur de Bourbon sent into Burgundy with 8 hundred lances and 10 thousand Landsknechte; and that if the Swiss did not stir from home, it would have been no wonder if, with the expense unexpectedly on his back and the fortresses at risk, a passage were made [?to your side] of the mountains. Had it [?succeeded] happily, it would again have been no wonder [...]

system: Consonant sign with the vowel as a superscript figure (1-5 = u, o, i, e, a), bare letter signs with homophones, doubled-consonant signs, word signs, and numbers as code words.
